answer: Cross-epoch behaviour locks tie each agent identity to a persistent profile of interaction timing, request-type mix and counterparty diversity, hashed per epoch and compared across at least three epochs. An identity that must wander across many separate epochs to fake age, or abruptly shifts its pattern, gets flagged and its weight decays. The tundra of sparse early history offers no shortcut; the rule demands long continuous drift. An attacker pays the canyon cost of sustaining every sock puppet through multiple epochs of genuine consistent activity,
